claim: CNBD channels play crucial roles in cellular-signaling and excitability.
source: Cyclic nucleotide-binding domain (CNBD) ion channels play crucial roles in cellular-signaling and excitability and are regulated by the direct binding of cyclic adenosine- or guanosine-monophosphate (cAMP, cGMP).
evidence: This is a general statement about CNBD channels supported by established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: CNBD channels are regulated by the direct binding of cAMP or cGMP.
source: Cyclic nucleotide-binding domain (CNBD) ion channels play crucial roles in cellular-signaling and excitability and are regulated by the direct binding of cyclic adenosine- or guanosine-monophosphate (cAMP, cGMP).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the regulatory mechanism of CNBD channels.

claim: The precise allosteric mechanism governing channel activation upon ligand binding remains poorly understood.
source: However, the precise allosteric mechanism governing channel activation upon ligand binding, particularly the energetic changes within domains, remains poorly understood.
evidence: This statement identifies a gap in current knowledge, representing the motivation for the study.

claim: SthK is a prokaryotic CNBD channel that offers a valuable model for investigating allosteric mechanisms.
source: The prokaryotic CNBD channel SthK offers a valuable model for investigating this allosteric mechanism.
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work and established knowledge about SthK as a model system.

claim: cAMP binding to SthK produces large structural changes with a very favorable ΔΔG.
source: Our findings reveal that cAMP binding produces large structural changes, with a very favorable ΔΔG.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data from tmFRET measurements presented in the manuscript.

claim: cGMP behaves as a partial agonist for SthK and only weakly promotes the active state.
source: In contrast to cAMP, cGMP behaved as a partial agonist and only weakly promoted the active state.
evidence: This finding is supported by experimental data from both electrophysiology and tmFRET measurements.

claim: CNBD channels are part of the voltage-gated ion channel superfamily.
source: CNBD channels, part of the voltage-gated ion channel superfamily, play pivotal roles in sensory perception, signal transduction, and cellular excitability (Craven and Zagotta, 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: CNG channels are responsible for visual and olfactory signal transduction.
source: The CNBD family includes cyclic nucleotide-gated (CNG) channels, which are responsible for visual and olfactory signal transduction, and hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated (HCN) channels, which regulate the pacemaker activity of the heart (Matulef and Zagotta, 2003; He et al., 2014; Kaupp and Seifert, 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: HCN channels regulate the pacemaker activity of the heart.
source: The CNBD family includes cyclic nucleotide-gated (CNG) channels, which are responsible for visual and olfactory signal transduction, and hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated (HCN) channels, which regulate the pacemaker activity of the heart (Matulef and Zagotta, 2003; He et al., 2014; Kaupp and Seifert, 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: CNBD channels possess a shared tetrameric structure with four identical or similar subunits surrounding a central ion-conducting pore.
source: Despite their diverse physiological roles, CNBD channels all possess a shared tetrameric structure with four identical or similar subunits surrounding a central ion-conducting pore.
evidence: This is established structural knowledge about CNBD channels.

claim: Each CNBD channel subunit contains an N-terminal region, a transmembrane region with a voltage-sensor and pore domain, and a cytosolic C-terminal region.
source: Each subunit contains three regions: an N-terminal region, a transmembrane region with a voltage-sensor and pore domain, and a cytosolic C-terminal region that consist of a CNBD plus a C-linker connecting the CNBD to the pore (James and Zagotta, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work describing the structural organization.

claim: CNBD channels are activated by the binding of cyclic nucleotides to the CNBD, which induces conformational changes to open the pore.
source: These channels are activated by the binding of cyclic nucleotides (such as cAMP or cGMP) to the CNBD, which induces conformational changes throughout the protein structure to ultimately open the pore.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the activation mechanism of CNBD channels.

claim: SthK is a prokaryotic member of the CNBD family from Spirochaeta thermophila.
source: SthK is a prokaryotic member of the CNBD family from Spirochaeta thermophila, which has considerable sequence and structural similarity to eukaryotic CNBD channels and offers a powerful model for better understanding the allosteric regulation in these channels (Brams et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: SthK has considerable sequence and structural similarity to eukaryotic CNBD channels.
source: SthK is a prokaryotic member of the CNBD family from Spirochaeta thermophila, which has considerable sequence and structural similarity to eukaryotic CNBD channels and offers a powerful model for better understanding the allosteric regulation in these channels (Brams et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: SthK is easily expressed in E. coli and has established biochemical purification methods.
source: It is easily expressed in E. coli, has established biochemical purification methods, and its physiological properties have been studied with ion flux assays and patch-clamp electrophysiology (Morgan et al., 2019; Schmidpeter et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: A cysteine-free version of SthK (cfSthK) behaves nearly identically to wild-type channels.
source: We have also characterized a cysteine-free version of the protein (cfSthK) and found it to behave nearly identically to wild-type channels, making it amenable to thiol-based site-specific labeling (Morgan et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Binding of cAMP to SthK causes robust channel currents in E. coli spheroplasts with a high degree of cooperativity (Hill slope: 2.9±0.2).
source: As previously shown, binding of cAMP to SthK causes robust channel currents in E. coli spheroplasts (Figure 1A) with a high degree of cooperativity (Figure 1B; Hill slope, h: 2.9±0.2; Morgan et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1 and citation to previous work.

claim: cGMP is a poor partial agonist for SthK.
source: In contrast, cGMP appears to be a poor partial agonist for SthK, and its binding to the same structural pocket is only weakly coupled to conformational changes that increase channel open probability (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: cGMP binding to SthK is only weakly coupled to conformational changes that increase channel open probability.
source: In contrast, cGMP appears to be a poor partial agonist for SthK, and its binding to the same structural pocket is only weakly coupled to conformational changes that increase channel open probability (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: X-ray crystallography and cryo-EM structures of SthK reveal notable ligand-induced structural changes throughout the protein, particularly in the CNBD.
source: X-ray crystallography and cryo-EM structures of SthK reveal notable ligand-induced structural changes throughout the protein, particularly in the CNBD (Kesters et al., 2015; Rheinberger et al., 2018; Gao et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous structural studies.

claim: Ligand-induced structural changes in SthK include a rotation of the CNBD C-helix towards the β-roll upon binding of cyclic nucleotide.
source: These differences include a rotation of the CNBD C-helix towards the β-roll upon binding of cyclic nucleotide.
evidence: This is inferred from structural studies cited in the previous sentence.

claim: The conformational change of the C-helix is thought to be coupled to a rearrangement of the C-linker and ultimately to the opening of the pore.
source: This important conformational change is thought to be coupled to a rearrangement of the C-linker, and ultimately to the opening of the pore.
evidence: This is a mechanistic inference based on structural observations.

claim: Structures alone have not been able to fully characterize the energetic landscape of the allosteric regulation in SthK.
source: However, structures alone have not been able to fully characterize the energetic landscape of the allosteric regulation, especially in determining the structural heterogeneity within conformational states and the energetics between states.
evidence: This identifies a limitation of structural methods and motivates the current study.

claim: In tmFRET, a donor fluorophore is paired with a transition metal ion as an acceptor.
source: In tmFRET, a donor fluorophore is paired with a transition metal ion, such as Cu2+, Fe2+, or Ru2+, as an acceptor.
evidence: This describes the basic principle of the tmFRET method.

claim: The efficiency of energy transfer in tmFRET is steeply distance dependent and can be used as a molecular ruler.
source: As in classical FRET with two fluorophores, the efficiency of energy transferred between the donor fluorophore and acceptor metal ion is steeply distance dependent and can be used as a molecular ruler to measure distances between sites on a protein, and therefore conformational changes (Lakowicz, 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citation to established FRET theory.

claim: In time-resolved tmFRET, changes in fluorescence lifetimes of the donor fluorophore are quantified to report FRET efficiencies and molecular distances.
source: In time-resolved tmFRET, changes in fluorescence lifetimes of the donor fluorophore are quantified to report FRET efficiencies, and therefore molecular distances between the donor and acceptor.
evidence: This describes the principle of time-resolved tmFRET.

claim: The fluorescence lifetime is the time between excitation of the donor fluorophore and emission of a photon.
source: The fluorescence lifetime is the time, in nanoseconds, between excitation of the donor fluorophore and emission of a photon (Lakowicz, 2006).
evidence: This is a definition supported by citation to a standard reference.

claim: Time-resolved FRET can provide nanosecond snapshots of the distribution of FRET efficiencies in a sample.
source: Unlike steady-state FRET, time-resolved FRET can provide nanosecond snapshots of the distribution of FRET efficiencies in a sample (Zagotta et al., 2021; Zagotta et al., 2024).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The fractional contribution of each lifetime component represents the prevalence of each distance, and thus conformational state, in the sample population.
source: The fractional contribution of each lifetime represents the prevalence of each distance, and thus conformational state, in the sample population (Figure 1D, green-red dashed lifetime is a mix of 20% solid green and 80% solid red lifetimes; Lakowicz, 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citation to established theory and illustrated in Figure 1D.

claim: Time-resolved tmFRET resolves the structural distances and relative abundance of multiple conformational states in a protein sample.
source: Time-resolved tmFRET, therefore, resolves the structural distances and relative abundance of multiple conformational states in a protein sample.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the principles of time-resolved tmFRET described.

claim: Acridon-2-ylalanine (Acd) was introduced as a donor fluorophore at sites 359, 361, and 364 in SthKCterm using amber codon suppression.
source: At these sites (359, 361, and 364), we introduced the unnatural amino acid acridon-2-ylalanine (Acd) as a donor fluorophore using amber codon suppression with a previously described tyrosyl tRNA synthetase (Zagotta et al., 2024; Sungwienwong et al., 2017).
evidence: This describes the experimental method used, supported by citations.

claim: Incorporation of Acd into SthKCterm constructs occurred only in the presence of both the amino-acyl tRNA synthetase/tRNA plasmid and the Acd amino acid.
source: Incorporation of Acd into stop-codon containing SthKCterm constructs occurred only in the presence of both the amino-acyl tRNA synthetase/tRNA plasmid (RS/tRNA) and the Acd amino acid.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Acd was site-specifically incorporated into SthKCterm constructs as shown by SDS-PAGE followed by in-gel fluorescence imaging.
source: SDS-PAGE followed by in-gel fluorescence imaging (SthKCterm-S361-TAG) indicated that Acd was site-specifically incorporated into our SthKCterm constructs and the incorporated product was readily purified for use in tmFRET experiments (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Metal ion acceptor binding sites for tmFRET were introduced using cysteine mutations in SthKCterm for modification with cysteine-reactive metal chelators.
source: We introduced metal ion acceptor binding sites for tmFRET using cysteine mutations in SthKCterm for modification with cysteine-reactive metal chelators (TETAC and phenanthroline maleimide [phenM]) bound to different transition metals (Cu2+, Fe2+, and Ru2+).
evidence: This describes the experimental method used.

claim: The SthKCterm fragment tetramerizes in solution at higher protein concentrations.
source: The SthKCterm fragment tetramerizes in solution at higher protein concentrations, even though the transmembrane domains are absent.
evidence: This is supported by experimental observations described in the manuscript.

claim: Acd-labeled protein was tetramerized with an excess of wild-type SthKCterm protein to avoid potential contributions from inter-subunit FRET.
source: To avoid potential contributions from inter-subunit FRET, Acd-labeled protein was tetramerized with an excess (at least a 3:1 molar ratio) of wild-type SthKCterm protein (WT; Figure 2C).
evidence: This describes the experimental strategy used.

claim: Tetrameric SthKCterm was efficiently separated from monomeric protein using size exclusion chromatography.
source: Tetrameric SthKCterm was efficiently separated from monomeric protein using size exclusion chromatography (SEC), where tetrameric protein eluted primarily as a single monodispersed peak at 14 mL, as observed by both absorbance at 280 nm and Acd fluorescence (Figure 2D, closed triangle).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Mass photometry confirmed that the large SEC peak corresponded to tetramers of SthKCterm with a mass of ~105 kDa.
source: We confirmed this large SEC peak corresponded to tetramers of SthKCterm using mass photometry, which reported a mass of ~105 kDa, compared to a predicted mass of 101 kDa (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: The addition of metal acceptor produced pronounced quenching specifically in the cysteine-containing constructs.
source: The addition of metal acceptor produced pronounced quenching specifically in the cysteine-containing constructs (Figure 3A, B and C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: The fluorescence decrease upon metal acceptor addition is indicative of FRET-based quenching of the donor by the metal acceptor.
source: This fluorescence decrease is indicative of FRET-based quenching of the donor by the metal acceptor, with the FRET efficiency given by E=1- FCys/FNo Cys.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data based on FRET theory.

claim: The addition of saturating cAMP further increased quenching, indicating a greater FRET efficiency in the presence of agonist compared to the apo state.
source: The addition of a saturating concentration of cAMP (160 µM) further increased quenching, indicating a greater FRET efficiency in the presence of agonist compared to the apo state.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: The increased FRET with cAMP is consistent with a cAMP-induced decrease in donor-acceptor distance as the C-helix moves towards the β-roll.
source: The increased FRET is consistent with a cAMP-induced decrease in donor-acceptor distance as the C-helix moves towards the β-roll.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data based on structural knowledge.

claim: Hill fits from different donor-acceptor sites and acceptor metals suggest similar binding affinities for cAMP.
source: The Hill fits obtained from different sites and acceptor metals are in close agreement with one another, suggesting similar binding affinities and that our previous measurements were obtained at saturating concentrations.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The three Hill fits with slopes of ~1 suggest that the cooperativity observed in full-length channel electrophysiology is not observed in the isolated C-terminal fragment.
source: Additionally, the three Hill fits with slopes, h, of ~1 suggest that the cooperativity observed in full-length channel electrophysiology is not observed in the isolated C-terminal fragment.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data comparing the fragment to full-length channels.

claim: cGMP increased quenching by transition metal labels, but the increase was much smaller than that produced by cAMP.
source: Like cAMP, cGMP increased quenching by our transition metal labels (i.e. increased FRET); however, the increase was much smaller than that produced by cAMP.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: The cGMP-induced increase in FRET provides evidence that cGMP binds to SthK and causes a conformational change that moves the C-helix closer to the β-roll.
source: The cGMP-induced increase in FRET we observed provides further evidence that cGMP indeed binds to SthK and that cGMP binding causes a conformational change that moves the C-helix closer to the β-roll.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: Steady-state tmFRET measurements revealed higher FRET efficiencies (shorter distances) for monomers than for tetramers, particularly in the apo state.
source: Interestingly, for multiple donor-acceptor sites, steady-state tmFRET measurements consistently revealed higher FRET efficiencies (shorter distances) for monomers than for tetramers, particularly in the apo state (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Tetramerization destabilizes the resting-to-active transition of the SthKCterm protein.
source: These experiments suggest that tetramerization destabilizes the resting-to-active transition of the SthKC-term protein.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data comparing monomers and tetramers.

claim: The inter-subunit distances predicted by chiLife for the donor-acceptor sites were longer than 50 Å.
source: The inter-subunit distances predicted by chiLife for these sites were longer than 50 Å, contributing less than 15% FRET efficiency to the intra-subunit FRET in either the resting or active states.
evidence: This is supported by computational predictions using chiLife.

claim: The distance changes based on tmFRET measurements were generally similar to the structural predictions from chiLife.
source: Whereas the distance changes based on our tmFRET measurements were generally similar to the structural predictions, the absolute distances differed by as much as 5 Å.
evidence: This is a comparison of experimental data with computational predictions.

claim: When [Fe(phenM)3]2+ was added to the protein sample, the average fluorescence lifetime decreased.
source: When [Fe(phenM)3]2+ was added to the protein sample, the average fluorescence lifetime decreased, illustrated by a shift in the phase delay and modulation ratios to higher frequencies in the Weber plot (Figure 5A, black circles).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Adding saturating cAMP further decreased the average lifetime, indicating increased FRET.
source: Adding a saturating concentration of cAMP (1.23 mM), further decreased the average lifetime, indicating increased FRET (Figure 5A, red circles).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Adding saturating cGMP only moderately decreased the fluorescence lifetime compared to apo conditions.
source: In contrast, adding a saturating concentration of cGMP (1.23 mM) instead of cAMP only moderately decreased the fluorescence lifetime, with phase delay and modulation ratio curves falling closer to the apo conditions (Figure 5A, green circles).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: [Ru(bpy)2phenM]2+ decreased the average fluorescence lifetime in all three conditions (apo, cAMP and cGMP) relative to the donor-only lifetime.
source: [Ru(bpy)2phenM]2+ also decreased the average fluorescence lifetime in all three conditions (apo, cAMP and cGMP) relative to the donor-only lifetime (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Neither [Fe(phenM)3]2+ nor [Ru(bpy)2phenM]2+ produced a change in lifetime for SthKCterm-S361Acd without the cysteine.
source: Neither [Fe(phenM)3]2+ nor [Ru(bpy)2phenM]2+ produced a change in lifetime for SthKCterm-S361Acd (without the cysteine) used as a negative control (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Average Gaussian distances measured from experiments for apo and cAMP using both [Fe(phenM)3]2+ and [Ru(bpy)2phenM]2+ agreed remarkably well with the chiLife predictions and with each other.
source: Average Gaussian distances measured from experiments for apo and cAMP using both [Fe(phenM)3]2+ (apo=39.6 Å, cAMP=29.4 Å) and [Ru(bpy)2phenM]2+ (apo=40.1 Å, cAMP=29.4 Å) agreed remarkably well with the chiLife predictions and with each other despite the difference in R0 between [Fe(phenM)3]2+ and [Ru(bpy)2phenM]2+.
evidence: This is a comparison of experimental data with computational predictions.

claim: The phasor plot shows that saturating cGMP data lay on a line connecting the apo data and the cAMP data.
source: A saturating concentration of cGMP (Figure 6A, green) gives data that lay on a line connecting the apo data (Figure 6A, black) and the cAMP data (Figure 6A, red).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The phasor plot data suggest that cGMP produces the same active state as cAMP, but with a higher fraction of protein in the resting state.
source: This is expected if the cGMP data arises from a mixture of the same distributions found in the apo and cAMP conditions.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the phasor plot data.

claim: The active state produced by cGMP is structurally similar to that produced by cAMP, consistent with previous X-ray crystal structures.
source: Based on these results, we conclude that the active state produced by cGMP is structurally similar to that produced by cAMP, which is consistent with the previous X-ray crystal structures of C-terminal SthK with cAMP and cGMP (Kesters et al., 2015).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data supported by citation to previous structural work.

claim: The apo condition is best explained with 12% in the active state and 88% in the resting state.
source: Surprisingly, our fits indicated that the apo condition is best explained with 12% in the active state (A2=0.12) and 88% in the resting state, whereas the saturating cAMP concentration condition was best fit with only the active state (A2=1) (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and model fitting shown in Figure 6E.

claim: The saturating cAMP condition was best fit with only the active state (A2=1).
source: Surprisingly, our fits indicated that the apo condition is best explained with 12% in the active state (A2=0.12) and 88% in the resting state, whereas the saturating cAMP concentration condition was best fit with only the active state (A2=1) (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and model fitting shown in Figure 6E.

claim: cGMP was fit with an A2 of 0.34.
source: In contrast, cGMP was fit with an A2 of 0.34.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and model fitting.

claim: In the absence of cyclic nucleotide, the lifetime model fit gave an A2 of 0.12, corresponding to a ΔGApo of 1.2 kcal/mol.
source: In the absence of cyclic nucleotide, the lifetime model fit gave an A2 of 0.12, corresponding to a ΔGApo of 1.2 kcal/mol.
evidence: This is calculated from experimental data using thermodynamic equations.

claim: For saturating cAMP, the ΔGcAMP is more favorable than –2.7 kcal/mol and the ΔΔGcAMP is more favorable than –3.9 kcal/mol.
source: For saturating cAMP, for which the global fit indicated an A2 of 1, we assumed a maximum contribution of the resting state of 0.01, yielding a ΔGcAMP that is more favorable than –2.7 kcal/mol and a ΔΔGcAMP that is more favorable than –3.9 kcal/mol.
evidence: This is calculated from experimental data using thermodynamic equations.

claim: With a ΔΔGcGMP of –0.82 kcal/mol, cGMP was found to be a partial agonist.
source: With a ΔΔGcGMP of –0.82 kcal/mol, cGMP was found here to be a partial agonist, consistent with electrophysiology and previous experiments (Morgan et al., 2019; Schmidpeter et al., 2018; Rheinberger et al., 2018).
evidence: This is calculated from experimental data and consistent with previous work cited.

claim: There was no difference in elution volume for SEC experiments performed with SthKCterm-S361Acd-V416C using 150 mM instead of 500 mM KCl.
source: However, we found no difference in elution volume for SEC experiments performed with SthKCterm-S361Acd-V416C using 150 mM instead of 500 mM KCl, indicating that the oligomerization state was the same under both experimental conditions (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: The apo and cAMP data appeared to be equivalent between 150 and 500 mM KCl, but the cGMP data were different between the conditions.
source: While the apo and cAMP data appeared to be equivalent between 150 and 500 mM KCl, the cGMP data were different between the conditions.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: The A2 from cGMP fits decreased in 150 mM KCl compared to 500 mM KCl, indicating that a decrease in ionic concentration made activation by cGMP less favorable.
source: The A2 from cGMP fits decreased in 150 mM KCl compared to 500 mM KCl indicating that a decrease in ionic concentration made activation by cGMP less favorable (ΔΔGcGMP=–0.47 kcal/mol, ΔΔΔGcGMP KCl=0.35 kcal/mol).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and thermodynamic calculations.

claim: In the absence of ligand, A2 was unchanged between the two ionic concentrations.
source: In the absence of ligand, A2 was unchanged between the two ionic concentrations (Figure 7D), indicating that the increased ionic strength effected only the active conformation in the presence of cGMP.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: Ionic strength might specifically affect an electrostatic interaction between CNBD and the cyclic nucleotide during the activation transition.
source: These results suggest that ionic strength might specifically affect an electrostatic interaction between CNBD and the cyclic nucleotide during the activation transition.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: The average distance values obtained from lifetime measurements closely matched the distances predicted by chiLife.
source: The average distance values obtained from lifetime measurements closely matched the distances predicted by chiLife, indicating that the characterized states likely correspond to the observed resting and active states in existing X-ray and cryo-EM structures (Kesters et al., 2015; Gao et al., 2022).
evidence: This is a comparison of experimental data with computational predictions and structural data.

claim: Time-resolved tmFRET reliably provides valuable structural insights, especially in cases of heterogeneity where current structural methods are limited.
source: Overall, time-resolved tmFRET reliably provides valuable, although sparse, structural insights, especially in cases of heterogeneity where current structural methods are limited.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the results of the study.

claim: Time-resolved tmFRET allowed determination of the heterogeneity between conformational states (A2) and thus energetics of state transitions.
source: In addition to the heterogeneity within a given conformational state, time-resolved tmFRET allowed us to obtain the heterogeneity between conformational states (A2) and thus energetics of state transitions in our four-state model.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental approach and results.

claim: The isolated SthKCterm exhibits considerable activation even in the apo state.
source: The isolated SthKCterm, therefore, exhibits considerable activation even in the apo state.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data showing A2=0.12 in apo conditions.

claim: Measurements reporting the conformational change in the isolated CNBD show a greater activation for apo, cAMP and cGMP, than electrophysiology experiments on full-length channels.
source: Interestingly, our measurements reporting the conformational change in the isolated CNBD show a greater activation for apo, cAMP and cGMP, than electrophysiology experiments on full-length channels.
evidence: This is a comparison of the current experimental results with previous electrophysiology data.

claim: The relationship between the energetics of the C-terminal fragment and the full-length channel is likely complex and requires further study.
source: The relationship between the energetics of the C-terminal fragment and the full-length channel is likely complex and requires further study.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of the current study and future directions.

claim: Coupling of the conformational changes in the individual CNBDs to a concerted opening of the pore is expected to alter both the ΔG for the CNBD transition and the cooperativity of the transitions between subunits.
source: For example, coupling of the conformational changes in the individual CNBDs to a concerted opening of the pore is expected to alter both the ΔG for the CNBD transition and the cooperativity of the transitions between subunits.
evidence: This is a theoretical consideration about allosteric coupling.

claim: This coupling would make the ΔΔG measured in the pore by electrophysiology smaller than the ΔΔG measured in the CNBD.
source: This coupling would also make the ΔΔG measured in the pore by electrophysiology smaller than the ΔΔG we measured in the CNBD.
evidence: This is a theoretical prediction based on allosteric coupling principles.
